By default the result is downloaded to the current directory. Override with `--output-dir ./out`, sk
Every model has an `API` tab on its detail page with the exact input schema. Browse the catalog:
| `--input '<JSON>'` | Inline JSON body. Strings can contain newlines; quote-escape as needed |
| `--input-file <path>` | Read body from a file (JSON or YAML by extension) |
| `--output-dir <path>` | Where to download result files (default: cwd) |
| `--no-download` | Skip the download step; only print the result JSON |
| `--no-wait` | Submit and return `request_id` immediately; don't poll |
| `--timeout <seconds>` | Cap the polling wait. Default: model-dependent |
| `--output json` | Print machine-readable JSON for piping (default human-readable) |
| `--quiet` | Suppress progress, keep only the final result line |

1. **Submit** — POSTs the JSON body to `model-api.runcomfy.net` with your bearer token.
2. **Poll** — GETs the request every ~2s until status is `completed`, `failed`, or `canceled`.
3. **Download** — for each output URL under `*.runcomfy.net` / `*.runcomfy.com`, fetch into `--outpu

content.user_title: Run RunComfy Models from the CLI
content.value_statement: Running RunComfy models from scripts can be hard to set up. This skill guides CLI installation, authentication, model calls, polling, and downloads.
actual_capabilities: Shows supported install paths for the RunComfy CLI.
Guides RunComfy login, token environment setup, and identity checks.
Explains how to run models with inline input or input files.
Covers no-wait jobs, status polling, JSON output, and downloads.
Lists relevant RunComfy catalog and documentation links.
Documents exit codes, retries, endpoint allowlists, and token handling.
limitations: Requires a RunComfy account and valid authentication token.
Requires the runcomfy CLI to be installed before model commands work.
Does not include every model schema; users must check each model API tab.
Generated media can incur service costs and remote processing time.

use_cases.title: Automate Model Runs
use_cases.description: Run image, video, edit, and training models from terminal workflows with saved outputs.

use_cases.title: Batch Generate Assets
use_cases.description: Process prompt lists, manage retries, and organize generated media into predictable folders.

use_cases.title: Integrate RunComfy Scripts
use_cases.description: Build scripted RunComfy workflows that submit jobs, poll status, and consume machine-readable results.

prompt_templates.title: Install and Verify
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me install the RunComfy CLI, sign in, and verify my account before running any model.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Use RunComfy to run a text-to-image model with my prompt and save the output to ./out.

prompt_templates.title: Submit and Poll Later
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a no-wait RunComfy job, capture the request ID, and show how I should poll status later.

prompt_templates.title: Build Batch Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a repeatable RunComfy batch workflow for prompts in a file, with retry handling and separate output folders.

output_examples.input: Run an image model for a product concept.
output_examples.output: The assistant selects a model, prepares the request, submits it with RunComfy, and reports the downloaded image location.
The assistant uses the request ID to check status and explains whether the job is queued, running, complete, or failed.
The assistant describes the batch steps, retry behavior, output folder plan, and where to review completed media files.

best_practices: Use verified package managers and inspect any remote install script before running it.
Keep RUNCOMFY_TOKEN out of prompts, logs, repositories, and shared transcripts.
Use explicit output directories so generated files are easy to review and clean.
anti_patterns: Piping remote install scripts into a shell without user review.
Uploading private assets or sensitive prompts to remote models without approval.
Enabling web search or third-party input ingestion when the task does not need it.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps an agent use the RunComfy CLI to run models, monitor jobs, and download outputs.

faq.question: Do I need a RunComfy account?
faq.answer: Yes. You need a RunComfy account and either an interactive login or RUNCOMFY_TOKEN.

faq.question: Can it run image and video models?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill covers RunComfy model endpoints for image, video, edits, lip-sync, face swap, and related tasks.

faq.question: Does it include every model input schema?
faq.answer: No. It directs users to each model API tab because schemas can differ across endpoints.

faq.question: Where are output files saved?
faq.answer: By default, files download to the current directory. The skill recommends explicit output folders.

faq.question: How should tokens be handled?
faq.answer: Store tokens only through the CLI or RUNCOMFY_TOKEN, and keep them out of logs, prompts, and repositories.
